removals.what: The flat fields of LetterboxdSyncResponse (added, removed, unmatchedTitles, pendingChoices, totalOnLetterboxd, totalTruncated and their watched twins), copies of what lists carries per list. ALLOWED_REMOVALS in scripts/check-contract-compat.mjs lets the contract drop them on the same date. Regenerate the contract with pnpm run openapi:sync
removals.why: The front of 1.31.1 and older reads them, deploy.yml publishes the API before the front, and a service worker keeps an old front for days: the API N serves the front N-1 (AGENTS.md, Compatible avec la version d'avant)

removals.what: The user document fields letterboxdLastSyncAt and letterboxdLastSyncError, still written next to letterboxdListSyncs and read as a fallback by LetterboxdListStatus.Of. For an account that has not synced since 1.32.1 the fallback holds its only sync date: copy it into letterboxdListSyncs by a migration, then stop writing and reading the two fields. UserProfileResponse keeps letterboxdLastSyncAt and letterboxdLastSyncError, derived from the per-list syncs, as long as a front reads them
removals.why: The API of 1.31.1 reads only these two fields: a revision of that version still serving, or brought back by a rollback, would show a stale sync date and error (AGENTS.md, Compatible avec la version d'avant)

removals.what: The request size limit RequestBodyLimits.AttachmentsBytes (25 MB) on the idea suggestion route, kept after the suggestions lost their attachments; the route falls back to the default limit. The Letterboxd import keeps its own use of the constant
removals.why: A front from before the attachments were removed, kept by its service worker, can still send screenshots and would get a 413 under the default limit: the API N serves the front N-1 (AGENTS.md, Compatible avec la version d'avant). The removal ships in the first release after v1.32.1

removals.what: The hostToken field of the old event documents: since DEBT-032 the API neither writes nor reads it, but every night created before still stores its token. Add RemoveEventHostTokensMigration in Infrastructure/Migrations, registered in DataMigrationServiceCollectionExtensions, an idempotent $unset of hostToken on the events matching { hostToken: { $exists: true } }, with a test against Mongo (pnpm run test:api:mongo); the entry ends once that registration exists. The host key of SENSITIVE_QUERY_PARAMETERS on the front and the host= filter of secret_urls in the cloud-run-api Terraform module can leave in the same change
removals.why: The API of 1.32.1 and older reads hostToken to let the holder of an old host link act as the host: a revision of that version still serving, or brought back by a rollback, would lose that access mid-way (AGENTS.md, Compatible avec la version d'avant). The API stops writing and reading the field in the first release after v1.32.1
